questions.def: Use 'the' before comparatives when they are parallel.
questions.question: ___ more I study, ___ more I learn.

questions.def: Use 'an' before a vowel sound, even in abbreviations.
questions.question: He is ___ accomplished musician.

questions.def: Omit 'a' before 'reason' when it's general knowledge.
questions.question: A reason for the delay is unknown.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'student' when referring to a specific field.
questions.question: She is ___ of art.

questions.def: Use 'the' with instruments; 'a' with a band.
questions.question: He plays ___ guitar in ___ band.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'unique' because of the consonant sound.
questions.question: This is ___ unique opportunity.

questions.def: Use 'the' with superlatives like 'best' (the best).
questions.question: She is a best player on the team.

questions.def: Use 'an' before 'example' because of the vowel sound.
questions.question: This is ___ of classic art.

questions.def: Use 'the' before unique or specific positions.
questions.question: ___ Prime Minister will address the nation.

questions.def: Use 'an' before 'honourable' because of the vowel sound.
questions.question: He is ___ honourable man.

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to a specific government.
questions.question: He works for ___.

questions.def: Use 'an' before 'expert'; 'the' for a specific field.
questions.question: She is ___ expert in ___ field.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'European' because of the consonant sound.
questions.question: He is ___ European.

questions.def: Use 'the' with 'most' when it means 'very'.
questions.question: This is a most interesting book I've read.

questions.def: Use 'an art' before 'critic' since it's a noun phrase.
questions.question: She is ___ critic.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'member'; 'the' for a specific committee.
questions.question: He is ___ member of ___ committee.

questions.def: Omit the article before general subjects like history.
questions.question: She wants to study ___ history.

questions.def: The article should be omitted in this context.
questions.question: He is the only person I know.

questions.def: Omit the article before general subjects like science.
questions.question: She is interested in ___.

questions.def: Use 'the' to refer to a group of people.
questions.question: ___ rich should help ___ poor.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'university' due to the consonant sound.
questions.question: He is ___ university professor.

questions.def: Use 'the' with 'only' to indicate uniqueness.
questions.question: She is a only child in her family.

questions.def: Omit the article before general subjects like law.
questions.question: He is studying ___.

questions.def: Use 'the' with superlatives and specific locations.
questions.question: He is ___ tallest in ___ class.

questions.def: Use 'an' before 'honest' because of the vowel sound.
questions.question: She is ___ honest person.

questions.def: Use 'the' before 'head' when referring to a specific role.
questions.question: He is a head of the department.

questions.def: Use 'a' + adjective (music) before a noun (teacher).
questions.question: She is ___ teacher.

questions.def: Use 'the' before comparatives in parallel constructions.
questions.question: ___ more you practice, ___ better you become.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'historian'.
questions.question: He is ___ historian.

questions.def: "Further" means "additional"; "farther" relates to physical distance.
questions.question: ___ more research is needed to confirm these findings.
